variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained to predict tokens in sequences. A token may be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or another encoded unit. During generation, the model repeatedly estimates what token should come next, samples or selects one, appends it to the context, and continues.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Follow the model through its full lifecycle”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Define and curate data
pairs.detail: Select lawful, relevant sources; remove harmful or low-value duplication; define mixtures, filters, provenance, and holdout boundaries.
pairs.explanation: Select lawful, relevant sources; remove harmful or low-value duplication; define mixtures, filters, provenance, and holdout boundaries.

pairs.label: Pretrain a base model
pairs.detail: Optimize token prediction over large corpora while tracking loss, data quality, compute use, contamination, and checkpoint health.
pairs.explanation: Optimize token prediction over large corpora while tracking loss, data quality, compute use, contamination, and checkpoint health.

pairs.label: Adapt behavior
pairs.detail: Use prompts, retrieval, supervised examples, or preference data to satisfy a task without making change more persistent than necessary.
pairs.explanation: Use prompts, retrieval, supervised examples, or preference data to satisfy a task without making change more persistent than necessary.

pairs.label: Serve token generation
pairs.detail: Schedule prefill and decode work, manage per-request attention state, enforce quotas, call tools, and validate outputs.
pairs.explanation: Schedule prefill and decode work, manage per-request attention state, enforce quotas, call tools, and validate outputs.

pairs.label: Evaluate and operate
pairs.detail: Gate versions on task, safety, latency, cost, and failure evidence; monitor drift and keep a tested rollback path.
pairs.explanation: Gate versions on task, safety, latency, cost, and failure evidence; monitor drift and keep a tested rollback path.

Output tokens are stored permanently in model weights.
Tokenization duplicates the model checkpoint for every request.
Attention removes all per-request state.
